title: Fire Instructor I
summary: Deliver prepared instruction: objectives, demonstration, coached practice, evaluation, safety, and records — without pretending to be the certification authority.

skills.title: Performance Objectives
skills.summary: Turn a station skill into one observable objective: who, does what, under what conditions, to what standard.
skills.whyItMatters: If the objective is ‘understand hose,’ nobody can teach it or test it. If it is ‘advance a charged 1¾-inch line to a marked door in full PPE,’ you can.
learningPoints: Observable verbs: don, advance, report, calculate — not ‘know’ or ‘appreciate.’
Conditions: PPE, lighting, staffing, props.
Standard: time, completeness, safety behaviors.
Instructor I often delivers prepared objectives — still know how to read and, if allowed, adjust them without breaking the standard.
beforeYouDo: Department lesson-plan template if you have one.

terminology.meaning: A measurable statement of what the learner will do.
A smaller step that supports the main performance.

safetyNotes: An objective that requires unsafe speed is a bad objective.
Live-fire objectives have extra rules — do not write those casually.

drill.objective: Write one performance objective for a company skill with conditions and a standard, then check it with a partner: could you evaluate it without guessing?
drill.equipment: Lesson topic, template or whiteboard, timer.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: Rewrite ‘understand SCBA’ into a performance statement.
debrief: How would you fail someone fairly?

15.title: 15-minute write
15.instructions: Three skills: knots, radio report, hydrant catch. One objective each.
debrief: Could a different instructor score this the same?

30.title: 30-minute micro-plan
30.instructions: Take one objective and list demo, practice, and the evaluation instrument.
commonMistakes: Test that does not match the objective
debrief: What safety constraint belongs in the conditions?

readinessQuestions.q: ‘The student will understand ventilation’ is a weak objective because:
Conditions in an objective tell you:
choices: The environment and constraints of the performance (PPE, props, staffing)

readinessQuestions.q: Instructor I using a prepared lesson plan should:
choices: Teach to those objectives unless the AHJ allows a documented adjustment that still meets the standard

skills.title: Deliver Prepared Instruction
skills.summary: Open, explain, check for understanding, and close — without drowning learners in slides.
skills.whyItMatters: A brilliant skill can still fail if the instructor rambles, skips the check, or never tells people what success looks like.
learningPoints: Open with the objective and why it matters on the job.
Chunk the explanation. Ask a real question.
Use the aid; do not read the aid.
Close by restating the performance they will do next.

terminology.meaning: A question or task that reveals whether the explanation landed — not ‘any questions?’ silence.

safetyNotes: Classroom delivery still needs a safety brief if you will move to a skill next.
Watch the clock. Fatigue creates accidents later on the drill ground.

drill.objective: Teach one narrow concept in 10 minutes with an opening, explanation, learner check, and close.
drill.setup: Pick a topic you already know. No new research rabbit holes.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: Write the opening sentence and the check question only.
debrief: What will you ask?

15.title: 15-minute micro-teach
15.instructions: Deliver 8 minutes plus 2 minutes of questions. Peer scores the four parts.
debrief: Did anyone besides the instructor talk?

30.title: 30-minute two teaches
30.instructions: Two instructors, two topics. Practice adapting when a learner is lost without abandoning the objective.
debrief: What will practice look like next?

readinessQuestions.q: ‘Any questions?’ after a lecture usually:
choices: Gets silence — ask a specific application question instead
readinessQuestions.why: Check with a prompt they can fail.

readinessQuestions.q: A visual aid should:
choices: Contain the entire lesson in 40 bullets
Support one idea at a time

readinessQuestions.q: If a learner is lost, Instructor I should:
choices: Adjust explanation/pacing inside the prepared lesson without changing the performance standard

skills.title: Demonstrate, Practice, Coach
skills.summary: Show the skill correctly, let them practice, and coach the next rep with specific feedback — then fade the prompting.
skills.whyItMatters: Talking about a ladder raise is not a ladder raise. Bad demos become departmental folklore.
learningPoints: Demonstrate at real speed, then slower if needed, with the same technique you will evaluate.
Learners need repetitions, not a second lecture.
Coach one or two things per rep, not twelve.
Safety stops the evolution immediately — then teach.
beforeYouDo: A familiar psychomotor skill and a prop.
The evaluation checklist you will eventually use.

terminology.meaning: Show the whole skill, break it into parts, then put it back together — one common method.

safetyNotes: Instructor demo must be the safe version, not the ‘street cheat.’
PPE for the skill is not optional because ‘it’s just training.’

drill.objective: Demonstrate a familiar skill, coach two learner reps with specific feedback, then watch a third rep with less talking.
drill.equipment: Familiar prop (knots, irons, packing a load), PPE as required, checklist.
drill.setup: Instructor is not the hero of the third rep.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: List the three errors you will watch for — only three.
debrief: What is unsafe vs ugly?

15.title: 15-minute coach
15.instructions: Demo once, two coached reps. Feedback = observed behavior + fix.
debrief: Did the second rep improve the thing you named?

30.title: 30-minute small group
30.instructions: Rotate learners. One safety officer. End with a standard-based pass/needs-more on the last rep (training only).
debrief: Does the last rep match the objective?

readinessQuestions.q: During practice the instructor should mostly:
choices: Watch and coach the actual performance
Perform the skill instead of the learner

readinessQuestions.q: Feedback works best when it is:
choices: Specific, timely, and limited to what they can fix on the next rep
readinessQuestions.why: Next rep is the test of the coaching.

readinessQuestions.q: If a learner is unsafe:
choices: Stop the skill, make it safe, then teach

skills.title: Training Safety Brief
skills.summary: Brief the evolution: objective, hazards, PPE, boundaries, stop signal, accountability, rehab, and the emergency plan.
skills.whyItMatters: Most training LODDs looked like ‘just a drill.’ The brief is how you refuse to be casual.
learningPoints: If you cannot name the emergency plan, you are not ready to start.
Stop signal must be known to every person on the ground, including students.
Live fire has additional, non-negotiable programs — do not run it off a vibe.
Accountability in training is still accountability.

terminology.meaning: How anyone halts the evolution for safety.
The person watching the whole problem, not performing the skill.

safetyNotes: NIOSH and USFA have documented training deaths. Read them. Do not copy the failures.

drill.objective: Deliver a 3-minute safety brief for a planned drill that includes stop signal, PPE, boundaries, and emergency action.
drill.equipment: Planned drill notes, cones for boundaries, radio.
drill.setup: Pick a non-live-fire drill unless you are in a compliant burn program — this product will not walk you into illegal live fire.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: Write the stop signal and who can use it (answer: anyone).
debrief: Where is the medical plan?

15.title: 15-minute brief
15.instructions: Give the brief. Peer checks for missing PPE, rehab, and accountability.
debrief: What is the boundary?

30.title: 30-minute run
30.instructions: Brief, run a short drill, then stop on a planted hazard. See if the stop actually works.
debrief: Would this brief have been enough at night?

readinessQuestions.q: Who may stop a training evolution?
choices: Anyone who sees an unsafe condition, using the briefed signal
readinessQuestions.why: If only one person can stop it, it will not stop in time.

readinessQuestions.q: Live-fire training:
choices: Can be improvised behind the station
Requires a compliant program, qualified instructors, and AHJ authorization — not a FireOpsSim drill card
Is the same as a kitchen fire

readinessQuestions.q: Accountability on the training ground:
choices: Is still required — you must know who is in the evolution
Is a clipboard problem for someone else
readinessQuestions.why: Lost students are still lost firefighters.

skills.title: Skill Evaluation
skills.summary: Give the same directions, watch the same points, score what you saw, and close professionally — this is not a popularity contest.
skills.whyItMatters: Inconsistent evaluators create unofficial standards and lawsuits. Fairness is a skill.
learningPoints: Read the instrument as written. Do not add secret extra fail points.
Watch the performance, not the reputation.
If you missed it, you cannot score it.
Remediation is part of the system, not a favor.
FireOpsSim quizzes are educational — they are not certification exams.
beforeYouDo: A sample skill sheet (department or training mock — not pirated NFPA text).
A learner to evaluate in a role-play.

terminology.meaning: A step that fails the skill if missed — per the issued sheet, not your mood.

safetyNotes: Stop unsafe evaluation performances the same as drills.
Do not evaluate live fire unless you are in that authorized program.

practiceResources.label: Firefighter Skills Checklist
practiceResources.note: Practice tracking — not an official sheet.

drill.objective: Run a mock skill evaluation: standard directions, silent observation, score, and a professional pass/needs-more closeout.
drill.equipment: Mock skill sheet, prop, two role-players (evaluator + student).
drill.setup: Use a FireOpsSim or department training sheet. Do not paste copyrighted standards.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: Read the sheet aloud. Highlight criticals. Agree you will not add extras.
debrief: What words start the eval?

15.title: 15-minute eval
15.instructions: One performance. Two evaluators score independently, then compare. Differences are the lesson.
commonMistakes: Coaching during a test if the sheet forbids it
debrief: Did we score reputation?

30.title: 30-minute eval + remediation
30.instructions: Fail a planted critical. Deliver the result, then a short remediation plan without rewriting the standard.
debrief: When is this an official cert test vs a training check?

readinessQuestions.q: During a scored evaluation, coaching the student:
choices: Depends on the rules of that test — many official tests forbid it
readinessQuestions.why: Instruction and evaluation are different modes. Know which you are in.

readinessQuestions.q: If two instructors score the same performance differently:
choices: The instrument or the training of evaluators needs work
Students should pick the better score

readinessQuestions.q: A FireOpsSim readiness quiz:
choices: Is educational feedback only — not an official examination
Should be put in the personnel file as certification

skills.title: Specific Feedback
skills.summary: Name the observed behavior, the standard, the effect, and the next repetition’s focus.
skills.whyItMatters: ‘Do better’ is not feedback. Neither is a personality review.
learningPoints: Observed > assumed.
One focus for the next rep.
Balance is not fake praise — it is accuracy.
Public feedback should not humiliate; safety stops are the exception.

terminology.meaning: A popular pattern that can hide the actual message — prefer clarity over ritual.

safetyNotes: Do not use humor that targets a person.
Immediate safety feedback can be blunt. Teaching feedback can then be precise.

drill.objective: After watching a skill, give 20-second feedback that names behavior, standard, and next-rep focus.
drill.setup: Switch roles. No real subordinates’ names.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: Rewrite ‘that was sloppy’ into an observed-behavior sentence.
debrief: What should they do next?

15.title: 15-minute rounds
15.instructions: Six mini-reps. Peer flags judgmental language.
debrief: Could they use it immediately?

30.title: 30-minute stubborn case
30.instructions: Learner repeats the same error. Practice escalating clarity without contempt, then a remediation decision.
debrief: Is this still instruction or is it evaluation?

readinessQuestions.q: The most useful feedback unit is:
choices: A specific observable action tied to the standard
A long story about when you were a recruit
readinessQuestions.why: They can only change what they can see.

readinessQuestions.q: ‘Good job’ with no detail:
choices: Does not tell them what to repeat
readinessQuestions.why: They do not know which part was good.

readinessQuestions.q: If the error is unsafe:
choices: Stop, make it safe, then give the teaching feedback

skills.title: Training Records
skills.summary: Complete attendance, objective, instructor, date/time, evaluation, and remediation fields so the record would survive an audit.
skills.whyItMatters: If it is not recorded, the organization cannot prove the training happened. That becomes a legal and ISO/accreditation problem.
learningPoints: Who was there, what was taught, who taught, when, and how it was evaluated.
Remediation and make-up sessions need the same dignity as the original.
Do not invent signatures.
FireOpsSim is not the department training record.

terminology.meaning: The official proof of instruction and evaluation — owned by the AHJ.

safetyNotes: Do not store student private data in FireOpsSim.
Live-fire and high-risk evolutions often have extra documentation — follow policy.

practiceResources.label: Firefighter Drill Builder
practiceResources.note: Plan fields you will later record.

drill.objective: Audit a messy de-identified training record and list every missing required field, then rewrite a clean closeout.
drill.equipment: Sample roster (fiction), department field list if available.
drill.setup: No real names or employee IDs.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: List the fields you would want if this became a lawsuit.
debrief: Where is the instructor name?

15.title: 15-minute audit
15.instructions: Find five defects in a bad record. Write the corrected line.
debrief: What about the person who left at lunch?

30.title: 30-minute closeout
30.instructions: Build a complete fictional record for today’s drill including one remediation.
commonMistakes: Optional fields skipped that policy requires
debrief: Which system does this actually get entered into on your job?

readinessQuestions.q: Attendance that is ‘everyone was there’ with no roster:
If a student failed and later passed a make-up:
choices: Record both per policy — the history is part of the record
Put it in FireOpsSim as official
readinessQuestions.why: Honesty in records is a legal skill.

readinessQuestions.q: FireOpsSim training notes are:
choices: A learning aid — the AHJ system is the record

officialSources.label: Department training-records SOP / accreditation rules
officialSources.scope: Retention, signatures, and required fields are local and legal.

skills.title: Adapt Delivery, Keep the Standard
skills.summary: Change explanation, pace, or demo for the learner in front of you without lowering the performance standard.
skills.whyItMatters: The job does not grade on a curve when the line is charged. Instruction can flex; the standard should not quietly disappear.
learningPoints: Some people need another demo. Some need to talk it. Some need a slower first rep.
Language, experience, and physical ability differ. The objective still stands unless the AHJ changes it.
Accommodation vs exemption is a policy issue — know when to refer.
Do not confuse being nice with being unclear.
beforeYouDo: Two learner profiles (e.g., experienced lateral vs brand-new recruit).

terminology.meaning: A allowed change in how they learn or demonstrate, not a secret easier standard — per policy.

safetyNotes: Do not adapt by removing PPE or skipping a safety step.
Fatigue adaptations still need the emergency plan.

drill.objective: Teach the same objective two ways for two learner profiles, then evaluate both against the same standard.
drill.equipment: Learner profile cards, one skill objective, prop.
drill.setup: Do not invent medical accommodations — refer those.
drill.disclaimer: Completing this drill does not satisfy an official certification task, skill sheet, or Roadmap Taskbook item.

5.title: 5-minute review
5.instructions: List three legal/safe adaptations (more demo, more reps, simpler language) and three illegal ones (skip PPE, skip criticals).
debrief: When do we call the training officer?

15.title: 15-minute two-path
15.instructions: Plan A for a nervous new member, plan B for a bored veteran. Same evaluation points.
commonMistakes: Letting the veteran skip the critical
debrief: Did both still get practice?

30.title: 30-minute live adapt
30.instructions: During a micro-teach, one learner is lost and one is ahead. Adjust without splitting the class into chaos.
debrief: What did we record for makeup?

readinessQuestions.q: Adapting a lesson means:
choices: Changing how you teach while keeping the required performance
readinessQuestions.why: Path can change. Destination should not vanish.

readinessQuestions.q: A veteran firefighter in class:
choices: Still owes the objective — they may need a different pace, not a free pass
Should teach instead of the instructor always

readinessQuestions.q: If a documented disability accommodation might apply:
choices: Follow department/academy official process — do not freelance medical decisions
Make them do extra PT as punishment
Discuss it with the whole class
